# [TASK] Implement start-tunnel.sh and stop-tunnel.sh scripts for local gateway exposure

## Task
Write scripts to launch and stop a local Cloudflare Tunnel container that prints the public HTTPS URL and publishes it for the deployed frontend to pick up.

## Scope
Includes `infrastructure/scripts/start-tunnel.sh` and `infrastructure/scripts/stop-tunnel.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `start-tunnel.sh` starts a `cloudflared` container (Docker or Podman, `--network host`) tunneling to `http://localhost:8080`, without requesting elevated privileges (`test_tunnel_scripts.TunnelScriptTest.test_start_tunnel_publishes_the_extracted_public_url`)
- [x] It extracts the public `https://*.trycloudflare.com` URL from the container's logs and writes it to `infrastructure/tunnel-url.txt` (`test_tunnel_scripts.TunnelScriptTest.test_start_tunnel_publishes_the_extracted_public_url`)
- [x] `stop-tunnel.sh` stops then removes the tunnel container (`test_tunnel_scripts.TunnelScriptTest.test_stop_tunnel_stops_then_removes_the_named_container`)
- [x] Against a real local gateway and a real Cloudflare quick tunnel, the printed URL answers `/actuator/health` (manual: `./gradlew deployLocal && ./gradlew startTunnel`, then `curl $(cat infrastructure/tunnel-url.txt)/actuator/health`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 2

## Notes
No sandbox this task has run in, including this one, has both a Docker daemon and network egress to Cloudflare, so the last criterion rests on evidence from the original implementation rather than a rerun here — same constraint as #229/#238/#250.
